title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Provisions on the Use of Court Gavels by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Provisions on the Use of the Court Gavel (Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2002] No. 1

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Provisions on the Use of the Court Gavel (Trial Implementation) were adopted at the 1201st meeting of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 24, 2001. The Provisions on the Use of the Court Gavel (Trial Implementation) are hereby issued to you. Please organize thorough study and implement them accordingly.

January 8, 2002

Provisions on the Use of the Court Gavel (Trial Implementation)

For the purpose of maintaining courtroom order and ensuring the normal conduct of judicial proceedings, the following provisions are formulated on the use of the court gavel:

Article 1. Judicial personnel of a People's Court shall use the court gavel when conducting trials in the courtroom.

When a case is tried under the ordinary procedure, the presiding judge shall use the court gavel; when a case is tried under the summary procedure, the sole judge shall use the court gavel.

Article 2. The court gavel shall be used under any of the following circumstances:

(1) when declaring the opening or resumption of a session;
(2) when declaring an adjournment or the conclusion of a session;
(3) when announcing a judgment or ruling.

Article 3. The court gavel may be used under any of the following circumstances:

(1) where a participant in the proceedings or a member of the audience violates the Rules of the People's Court Courtroom, obstructs the trial, or disturbs courtroom order;
(2) where a participant in the proceedings makes statements irrelevant to the case or repeats statements;
(3) other circumstances where the presiding judge or the sole judge deems it necessary to use the court gavel.

Article 4. The court gavel shall be placed in front of the bench of the presiding judge or the sole judge.

Article 5. The procedure for using the court gavel by the presiding judge or the sole judge is as follows:

(1) when declaring the opening or resumption of a session, strike the gavel first, then declare the opening or resumption;
(2) when declaring an adjournment or the conclusion of a session, declare the adjournment or conclusion first, then strike the gavel;
(3) when announcing a judgment or ruling, announce the judgment or ruling first, then strike the gavel;
(4) when using the gavel under other circumstances, strike the gavel first, then give instructions on the progress of the trial.

When the presiding judge or the sole judge uses the gavel, it shall generally be struck once.

Article 6. Upon hearing the sound of the gavel, participants in the proceedings and members of the audience shall immediately cease speaking and any conduct that violates courtroom rules; if they continue such conduct, the presiding judge or the sole judge may, depending on the circumstances, take measures in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Rules of the People's Court Courtroom.

Article 7. The court gavel shall be manufactured under the supervision of the Supreme People's Court.

Article 8. These Provisions (Trial Implementation) shall take effect on June 1, 2002.
